articleTitle: Millimeter Wave and Other Circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs MMICs are being used in applications at frequencies ranging from DC to greater than 100 GHz. The inherent advantage of monolithic circuits over conventional hybrid circuits in the area of the control of parasitics, coupled with the rapid advancements in the area of millimeter-wave active components, are now being demonstrated in the performance of millimeter-wave circuits. At lower frequencies, GaAs circuits are bridging the interface between the traditional microwave and digital applications where differing functions will be integrated in systems.

articleTitle: Testing and Packaging
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Testing and packaging of GaAs ICs represent important strategic issues affecting timely insertion of GaAs technology in many commercial and military product/component areas. Many of the GaAs ICs under development today will form the building blocks for tomorrow's most sophisticated high speed test equipment. All types of GaAs ICs will require advanced packaging concepts to realize full performance in integrated systems. In addition, non-destructive, non-invasive chip/device level testing schemes offer attractive tools for development and characterization of today's GaAs ICs.

articleTitle: Integrated-Circuit Fabrication Technology
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs integrated circuit technology has matured at a rapid rate during the last few years. Device performance, circuit complexity and fabrication yields have all improved significantly during this period. The papers in this session extend this trend in several important areas. Two papers present new insights into the impact of ion-implantation on MESFET performance and uniformity. Two more papers propose novel high performance gate processes for LSI E/D MESFET circuits. Finally, one paper describes a new self-aligned process for heterojunction bipolar transistors.

articleTitle: Digital Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Continued growth is occurring across a broad range of LSI-III-V digital ICs. This session highlights advances in both instrumentation ICs and high-speed SRAMS. Also considered are performance issues related to layout parasitics.

articleTitle: Materials
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: High yield GaAs MSI and LSI circuits are being fabricated successfully today because of continued improvements In bulk-and epitaxial-material technologies. The role of various types of GaAs substrate dislocations and impurities and their impact on device parameters are discussed in the first three papers of this session. Finally, MBE-grown GaAs/Si bipolar and FET devices are presented with a discussion of the feasibility of this approach to future ICs.

articleTitle: Microwave Power and Control Circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Monolithic amplifiers delivering power over a broad range of frequencies continue to be an extremely important application of GaAs. The papers in this session begin with a review of recent results at X and Ka bands followed by design layout considerations and push-pull performance at X-band. Lower frequencies are represented by descriptions of two wideband phase shifters across C, X and Ku bands. Examples of some of the special techniques that are evolving in this field are an X-band electronically stabilized monolithic source using analog dividers and a tapered, distributed amplifier that covers 1-10 GHz.

articleTitle: Reliability and Circuit Applications
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Application of GaAs IC components is an ultimate goal in the development of this technology. Highlighted in this session are two papers describing GaAs IC components for a TV tuner application and a sensor application. A third paper describes a GaAs IC system application utilizing several different GaAs IC chips. A central question to be answered in ali these applications is the reliability of GaAs ICs. A fourth paper in this session focuses on some reliability investigations of GaAs IC components.

articleTitle: Digital Integrated Circuits (I)
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Digital GaAs ICs are coming of age with the advent of a number of commercial suppliers and foundry services. This session details a variety of recent high-performance applications-oriented circuits produced by these and other sources. It also covers guidelines for the selection of GaAs ICs among competing technologies In a given application area, and examines the status of the emerging, very high performance technologies based on (Ga,Al)As/GaAs heterostructure devices.

articleTitle: Advances in GaAs Monolithic Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: GaAs monolithic power amplifiers have been under development since the late 1970s. Most of the initial work was done at X-band frequencies, but recently there has been significant progress at frequencies as high as 28 GHz. This paper will cover the current status of GaAs monolithic power amplifiers and projections of their future performance capability.

articleTitle: A GaAs Multi-Band Digitally-Controlled 0° - 360° Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A monolithic GaAs active phase shifter is demonstrated over UHF, L-, S- and C-bands. This device, in combination with a hybrid 90-degree coupler, can generate phase shift from 0 to 90 degrees in 11.25-degree steps. The phase shifts can be digitally programmed within 2 degrees in a narrow band application. The maximum phase errors are within 5 degrees, with the maximum amplitude variations no more than 2.5 dB among various phase states at frequencies from 1 to 8 GHz. The fabricated chip size is 45 × 45 × 20 mils. Applications for multi-band and multi-octave phase shifters are discussed.

articleTitle: A X-Band 4.5 Watt Push-Pull Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A GaAs monolithic push-pull power amplifier has been developed which generates 4.5 Watts of output power at 9.5 GHz. This single chip amplifier consists of two 3-staqe power amplifiers driven by a paraphase splitter. The chip dimensions are 6.7 mm × 5.0 mm. This 4-stage amplifier exhibits a large signal gain of 16 dB with a power added efficiency of 15%. The small signal gain is 21.5 dB over a 1.2 GHz bandwidth.

articleTitle: 11GHz Band GaAs Monolithic VCO with 1/4 Analog Frequency Divider
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An 11 GHz band GaAs monolithic voltage controlled oscillator (VCO) and divide-by-four analog frequency divider have been developed. The VCO has a series feedback configuration and utilizes an optimized design procedure to yield 28% dc-RF efficiency, which is believed to be the state-of-the-art data for a GaAs monolithic FET oscillator. The frequency divider, on the other hand, has a novel structure which mainly applies a dual gate FET mixer and two RC coupled FET inverter stages to estabilish a closed loop for generating a 1/4 subharmonic component of an input frequency. Performance for the frequency divider, estimated by a SPICE simulation, is in good agreement with experimental results. Operation of the divider when driven by the VCO, promises applicability of the circuits developed to realization of a stable local source in a Phase-locked loop system.

articleTitle: A 115 GHz Monolithic GaAs FET Oscillator
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A monolithic GaAs FET oscillator with an operating frequency as high as 115 GHz has been demonstrated. A 75 µm × 0.2 µm GaAs FET with monolithic feedback and matching elements was used for the oscillator design. The chip size is 28 mils × 35 mils × 4 mils.

articleTitle: A 30 GHz Monolithic Two Stage Low Noise Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Combining improved ion implantation technology, optimized high frequency FET design, sub-half-micron gate fabrication and accurate modeling of MMIC components at millimeter-wave frequencies, we have developed a monolithic LNA operating at 30 GHz. The amplifier has a measured gain greater than 14 dB, with a noise figure of 7 dB. This is the first monolithic LNA operating at Ka-band reported to date.

articleTitle: GaAs Differential Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper presents the design, analysis, and experimental results of a wide bandwidth differential amplifier, suitable for integrated circuit (IC) applications, fabricated in D-MESFET GaAs technology. Increased tolerance to process variations is achieved by a local feedback technique that stabilizes the operating point in the high gain region. A Monte Carlo analysis technique was employed to estimate differential amplifier offset and then to predict A/D converter resolution as a function of process uniformity. The amplifier demonstrated a mean offset of 2.6 mV with a standard deviation of 69.4 mV. The mean dc gain was 22 dB with a maximum of 26 dB. The amplifier demonstrated 17 dB of gain at 500 MHz with a 150 fF load and an estimated bandwidth of over 4 GHz under typical IC conditions. Trap-related performance degradation contributed to decresed amplifier gain above 10 MHz and frequency dependent hysteresis.

articleTitle: Direct Electro-Optic Sampling of Analog and Digital GaAs Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: We report the first electro-optic sampling measurements made directly in integrated circuits. Both monolithic microwave integrated circuits and medium-scale-integrated digital circuits operating at gigahertz frequencies have been non-invasively probed by combining the electro-optic effect in GaAs with sub-bandgap (1.06 μm) picosecond pulses from a continuous-wave (cw) mode-locked Nd:YAG laser. Digital circuits are probed using a new backside reflecting geometry, in which a laser beam enters the substrate from the back and reflects from the circuit metallization. We present measurements made on the 2 μm wide, on-chip output line of a multiplexer/demultiplexer clocked at 2.6 GHz, and on the gate and drain lines of a traveling wave amplifier up to 26 GHz.

articleTitle: Reliability Investigation of GaAs IC Components
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Reliability tests have been conducted on MESFETs, MIM capacitors, NiCr resistors, interconnect metallization, and ring oscillators fabricated using TriQuint's 1-micron depletion mode manufacturing process. The observed MTTF (median time to failure) for FETs is 80 hours at 290 degrees C channel temperature, with an activation energy of 1.6 eV. Parameter drift data from 1000 hour lifetests on FETs, NiCr resistors, interconnect metallization, and ring oscillators are presented. Also presented are results of ESD sensitivity tests on digital IC inputs.

articleTitle: 1 GHz Sample Rate GaAs CCD Transversal Filter
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Substantial progress towards the incorporation of a 1 GHz continuous clock rate GaAs CCD in a monolithic transversal filter design has been achieved. This is the first report of such a high sample frequency transversal filter. The present design provides filter performance in the VHF/UHF region, up to 500 MHz, with input sampling in excess of 1 GHz. At 1 GHz continuous sampling the filter response displays a linear dynamic range in excess of 60 dB for all three filter functions: band pass and switchable high pass or low pass.

articleTitle: Microwave Chip Carrier for Monolithic Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Small, multiport microwave chip carriers which were designed to address the packaging needs of monolithic microwave integrated circuits are described. These chip carriers have been tested through 20 GHz and have demonstrated insertion loss into the package of 0.25 dB, return loss of 20 dB at all ports, and isolation between adjacent signal paths of better than 30 dB. The standard packages have either 20 or 24 I/O ports, metal to ceramic hermetic sealing, and heat transfer capabilities of 2 watts. The 0.050 inch spacing of signal paths on the outside of the package results in a chip carrier which is easily mounted in most microwave packaging schemes. These attributes of the microwave chip carriers, combined with their small size and weight and low cost, make them ideal for high speed, high frequency monolithic applications.

articleTitle: A High-Temperature Sensor Based on Monolithic GaAs Hall IC
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A high-temperature position sensor has been developed wfiich is based on a monolithic GaAs Hall IC. The three-stage Hall IC contains a Hall device with constant current source, a dual-gate MESFET differential amplifier and a source-follower. The differential amplifier delivers a low-frequency gain up to 350, the Hall MIC a sensitivity up to 180 V/Tesla. The main application is in automobile electronics, where in a high-temperature environment ($$ 180 C) a local amplification of the sensor signal is necessary with respect to high noise level. A new key technology with the synonym DIOM will be described, which ful fills simultaneously the reliability requirements of the sensor and the gain and uniformity demands of the differential amplifier.

articleTitle: Low-Resistivity W/WSix Bila YER Gates for Self-Aligned GaAs Mesfet LSIs
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The W/WSi<inf>x</inf> bilayer gate structure was newly developed for realizing high performance GaAs LSIs. It was experimentally found that W/WSi<inf>x</inf> bilayer with 0.1 μm thick WSi<inf>0.</inf>4 film is useful from low resistivity and stable Schottky barrier characteristics points of view. 18 μΩ·cm average resistivity, which is one order of magnitude lower than that for the WSio.4 single layer, was obtained for W/WSio.4 bilayer film with 0.5 µm total film thickness. High performance FET characteristics were confirmed for n<sup>+</sup> self-aligned W/WSi<inf>0.4</inf> bilayer gate MESFETs.

articleTitle: High Performance Mesfet Technology for GaAs ICs using Shallow n-Channels
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A comprehensive experimental study on GaAs MESFETs design principle has been made. With the fabrication process for WSi<inf>x</inf> - gate self-aligned MESFETs, performance has been improved by a factor of 2 through reduction of implant energy from 75 to 40 keV. Transconductance coefficients, K, as high as 2 mA/V<sup>2</sup> for EFETs and 1.2 mA/V<sup>2</sup> for DFETs have been attained at 1 µm gate length and 10 µm channel width, which are one of the highest ever reported. Consistent, fundamental data on K values and gate capacitance have been obtained. High performance MESFETs have been used successfully in a 4-Kb GaAs SRAM experiment.

articleTitle: GaAs Monolithic Digital Phase/Frequency Discriminator
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A GaAs monolithic digital phase/frequency discirminator with a linear characteristic at the zero phase crossing has been developed at Hughes SCG. The maximum operating frequency of 480 MHz is about ten times faster than that of existing silicon devices. These devices are currently used in low noise phase-locked loops. We discuss the design, operation, and use of this device.

articleTitle: Small Access Time Scattering GaAs SRAM Technology using Bootstrap Circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A circuit technology which has made it possible to realize a high speed GaAs SRAM with small access time scattering is described. The principal cause of the access time scattering is analysed and for the first time is clarified to be data-line signal amplitude scattering in the memory cell array. The bootstrap circuits introduced to shorten the transient time of the data-line signal are proven to be effective in reducing the access time scattering by more than 50%. An ECL-compatible 1KWx4b GaAs SRAM has been designed and fabricated using this technology. Access time of 2.6ns(typ.) with 890mW power dissipation has been achieved. Normal read/write operation at 4ns cycle time has also been confirmed.

articleTitle: Non-Uniformity in In-Doped/Alloyed, Semi-Insulating GaAs
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Large scattering in the sheet carrier concentration (N<inf>s</inf>) of the Si-implanted layer, that determines threshold voltage for field-effect transistors, is found around dislocations even in In-doped/alloyed, semi-insulating GaAs. Dislocations affect N<inf>s</inf> within about a 75 µm radius area and the carrier concentration increases 2 × 10<sup>15</sup> cm<sup>-3</sup> per dislocation in this area. N<inf>s</inf> scattering drastically decreases in the completely dislocation-free, 2-in-diameter crystal. N<inf>s</inf> standard deviation ($$N<inf>S</inf>) was 0.15 × 10<sup>11</sup> cm<sup>-2</sup> ($$N<inf>s</inf>/N<inf>s</inf>$$2.5%). This value is 1/5 of that for the conventional dislocated crystal. In-doped/alloyed, dislocation-free crystals are promising for realizing high performance GaAs-LSI substrates.

articleTitle: Time Simulation of Fast GAAS Logic Circuits with Their Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: BFL and DCFL GaAs logia cirouit configurations are investigated with their transmission lines. A new time simulator MACPRO gives a precise evaluation of signal degradations related to the propagation of retroaotions and coupling effects in picosecond circuits.

articleTitle: A Fully Operational 1Kb HEMT Static RAM
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Improvements in materials and process and design technologies are discussed in terms of realizing fully operational HEMT LSIs. Technology to guarantee highly uniform device parameters has been established. Cell stability has been investigated for variations in device characteristics. Fully operational HEMT 1Kb SRAMs have been confirmed under marching tests and partial galloping tests. The RAM chips have also shown excellent uniformity in access time. The difference between maximum and average values on the RAM chip is 4%.

articleTitle: Prospects for the Monolithic Integration of GaAs and Si
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: We have studied the properties of GaAs FETs and BJTs grown on Si substrates by molecular beam epitaxy. In GaAs MESFETs grown on Si, very small sidegating magnitudes were obtained with less than a 10% reduction in drain current when a -5V is applied to a side gate pad located 3µm from the device. We have also demonstrated the feasibility of monolithically integrating GaAs and Si devices by fabricating MODFETs with excellent characteristics on a Si wafer which has NMOS devices, with no degradation in performance. GaAs homojunction bipolar transistors with a base width of 0.2µm grown on Si exhibited common emitter current gains of β=9. demonstrating very good minority carrier properties in this material. Current densities of 105.000A/cm<sup>2</sup> were obtained without deterioration of the device demonstrating the excellent stability of this material. These results have important implications as to the future role of GaAs in integrated circuits.

articleTitle: High Speed Manchester Decoding using GaAs D-Mesfet ICs.
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper examines the use of digital GaAs IC's in the receiver portion of a bus interface unit (BIU) that is being developed to connect to an electrical high-speed data bus (HSDB). The receiver includes a GaAs Manchester decoder and 100K ECL circuits for serial to parallel data conversion. The decoder consists of a 300 equivalent gate, GaAs cell array along with standard MSI digital GaAs D-MESFET IC's (four-bit universal shift register, divide by 2/4/8 binary counter). The GaAs chip set decodes 100 Mbit/s Manchester II encoded data. The cell array has been designed and fabricated. Functional testing of the cell array has shown working parts on the first iteration with a 20% yield. Incoming asynchronous Manchester II data is oversampled and processed using a 1.25 ns cycle time. The cell array outputs differential NRZ data and clock along with an error detect bit.

articleTitle: A Guide to Integrated Circuit Technology Comparisons
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper presents a simple guide to integrated circuit technology comparisons with emphasis on constraints dictated by the intended application. The technologies to be considered are III-V MESFET, Si MOS, Si bipolar, and III-V bipolar. Some comments will also be made on technology comparisons specific to linear and low noise applications.

articleTitle: A High-Speed 4×4 Bit Parallel Multiplier using Selectively Doped Heterostructure Transistors
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 4×4 bit parallel multiplier using selectively doped heterostructure transistors (SDHT) has been demonstrated. The circuit was implemented with NOR gates using direct coupled FET logic (DCFL). The shortest propagation delay was measured to be 114ps/gate which corresponds to a multiplication time of 1.6ns. At this speed the circuit dissipated .34mW/gate. This is the best result ever reported for a parallel multiplier at room temperature.

articleTitle: High-Speed, High-Accuracy Voltage Comparators Implemented with GaAs/(GaAl)As Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The first voltage comparators implemented with GaAs/(GaAl)As heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) are reported. On a quasi-static basis, the offset voltage was found to be generally below 4 mV, and hysteresis about 1 mV. The HBT comparators could be clocked at frequencies above 2.5 GHz. They operated over a range of reference voltage of 2 V. The preliminary yield was high. These results indicate that the HBT comparators are suitable for flash analog-to-digital converters with up to 8 bit accuracy, and sampling rates well above 1 GHz.

articleTitle: L-Band GaAs Transceiver Components
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The development of three GaAs MMIC's for L-Band Radar Transceiver (T/R) applications has been accomplished. The three chips are a 5-bit phase-shifter, a 3-stage 1-watt power amplifier and a 3-stage low noise amplifier. The transmit/receive switching functions are included as part of the individual designs. These MMIC designs demonstrate the feasibility of using 2 um gates for both power amplifier and low noise amplifier functions at L-Band, which reduces the processing complexity and allows both amplifier designs to be processed on a single GaAs wafer. This allows for the possibility of integrating the power amplifier and low noise amplifier into a single chip as the processing yields improve. Performance and processing yield data for each of the individual MMIC's is presented.

articleTitle: Half-Watt X-Band Amplifier Tests Layout Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 1/2 Watt X-Band single ended monolithic amplifier was designed using both small and large signal modelling. The amplifier consists of a 600 μm FET driving a 1200 µm FET on a 74 × 104 × 4 mil chip. All capacitors are Si<inf>3</inf>N<inf>4</inf>, resistors are Ti/Pt. Gate length is 0.85 μm, gates are written by Ε-beam. Although intended for narrow band operation, the design was extended to a 3 GHz bandwidth to allow for frequency shifts due to process variations. An experimental mask set was fabricated with four variations of the amplifier design. This accomplished two purposes: the performance sensitivity to layout variations was tested, and the need to lengthen certain transmission lines to compensate for coupling, line bends and junction effects was demonstrated. Results from several wafers of the experimental mask show that the chosen design is tolerant to significant wafer to wafer and DC parameter variations. Amplifiers have been produced on both implant and epitaxial material. Best results to date are 600 mW output power at 10 dB gain, with small signal gain of 12 to 14 dB. Efficiency as high as 35 percent at 500 mW has been observed. Input and output matches are typically better than 10 dB over a bandwidth of approximately 3 GHz.

articleTitle: Monolithic 6-18 GHz 3 Bit Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 6-18 GHz 3 bit GaAs MMIC phase shifter is described. It incorporates novel high-pass/low-pass circuit structures, with 0.7 µm gate length MESFETs as switching elements. MESFET off-state capacitances are incorporated as. circuit elements, and need not be resonated, thus broadband performance is readily achieved. Each of the 3 bits (45°, 90°, and 180°) has a unique topology, chosen for optimal performance for its specific phase shift. The total FET gate periphery for all 3 bits is 4.9 mm. The 3 bit chip measures only 49 by 87 mils, and is on a 4 mil GaAs substrate.

articleTitle: A 1 to 10 GHz Tapered Distributed Amplifier in a Hermetic Surface Mount Package
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 1 to 10 GHz monolithic GaAs distributed amplifier with a tapered drain line has been developed with greater than 7 dB gain. Input and output VSWR's are better than 2.5:1. One dB gain compressed power exceeds +18 dBm. The tapered drain line provides a design topology to increase the efficiency of distributed amplifiers. The utility of the amplifier was enhanced by the use of a controlled impedance, surface mount package.

articleTitle: Monolithic Millimeter-Wave Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper summarizes the progress, trends, and technical issues associated with GaAs-based monolithic millimeter-wave effort. Presented first is background information intended to set forth: a description of the opportunities which spur this effort; and a summary of some of the important technical challenges. Next, a discussion is provided of the semiconductor device types and circuit media which serve as building blocks for this technology. Then a description is provided of salient monolithic programs which benchmark the status of current effort. The paper concludes with a summary of technical issues and thrusts.

articleTitle: A 2 to 40 GHz Monolithic Distributed Amplifier
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A monolithic distributed amplifier (DA) which operates from 2 to 40 GHz is presented. The device has a gain of 4 dB over the entire band with a noise figure of less than 9 dB in K-band and 7 dB at 10 GHz. The output power at 1 dB compression is +12 dBm. Two chips were cascaded to achieve 8 dB gain from 2 to 40 GHz. The seven-section circuit has 476 μm total gate periphery and is fabricated on a 1.1 × 3.2 mm chip.

articleTitle: Requirements and Interim Solutions for High-Speed Testing of GaAs ICs
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The test system requirements for GaAs digital ICs are identified. The main limitations of the presently available automated testers are the generation and acquisition of gigabit rate test patterns with high accuracy, and the test-fixtures required to probe wafers and packaged components. Solutions to the above limitations are now becoming available in the form of GaAs ICs such as high-speed Static RAMs and 2-3 GHz rate MUX/DEMUX ICs and novel test-fixture techniques based on polyimide flexible circuits, elastomers and gold- dot connectors. Several interim test techniques must be employed until these techniques become commercially available at reasonable costs. One of the nost cost-effective test technique is to use D.C. testing prior to H.S. test to screen out the three most common failure nodes i.e. defects, inadequate noise margins, and poor transconductance of MESFETs. Correlation between high-speed performance and such parameters as ring-oscillator speeds, MESFET transconductance, power supply current levels can also be used to minimize the dependence on the high-speed testers and thus cut the cost of testing the GaAs ICs. Finally some novel on-chip test techniques are discussed.

articleTitle: A GaAs Switched-Capacitor Bandpass Filter IC
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This work is concerned with attempts to implement switched-capacitor techniques in GaAs technology. A two-pole bandpass filter has been designed and fabricated, and operation with switch frequencies up to 250 MHz and centre frequencies up to 10 MHz has been achieved. This performance puts standard switched-capacitor techniques well into the megahertz range which will allow their use in applications such as clock recovery in data communications systems, agile filtering for radar and communications receivers, and video processing in television receivers. A higher level of integration in these systems may thus be achieved than has been possible in the past.

articleTitle: New Approaches to Packaging for High Speed GaAs IC Applications
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Gallium arsenide integrated circuits offer the potential for very high speed operation, but only if the performance is not compromised by packaging considerations. It is already widely recognized that this will require innovations beyond currently available designs, particularly for digital circuits with high signal pin counts. This paper summarizes work performed during the last two years targeted to provide solutions to the problem of packaging high speed GaAs digital circuits operating at clock rates from 500 MHz to several GHz. Two approaches to packaging discrete devices are described, as well as the fabrication of a multi-chip hybrid incorporating 6 GaAs ICs and operating at clock rates up to 3 gigabits per second.

articleTitle: GaAs Monolithic Circuits for TV Tuners
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: An hybrid GaAs TV tuner including a monolithic down converter (local oscillator and mixer) has been realised and evaluated in the UHF band. Various types of local oscillators and mixers have been considered. The overall performance of the tuner is 25 dB conversion gain with 10 dB noise figure.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Oscillations in GaAs IC's
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: Anomalous peaks in the phase noise of a GaAs IC dynamic divider are correlated to oscillations in the leakage currents in the semi-insulating GaAs substrate. The low-frequency oscillations in both substrate and FET currents and the excess phase noise in the divider exhibit similar dependence upon bulk GaAs material. Mechanisms by which oscillating substrate leakage currents modulate the FET are presented and correlated to the dependence of phase noise on IC layout.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of a Digital RF Memory using Custom Designed GaAs Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper describes the design constraints which required solution during the implementation of a mixed Gallium Arsenide/silicon ECL Digital RF Memory (DRFM). This unit, which is configured to digitize an analog signal at 1 GHz rates, has served as a test bed for ten separate designs for the high clock rate front and back ends of the DRFM system. Preliminary test results from the GaAs components are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: The Effect of Channeling on the LSI-Grade Uniformity of GaAs-FETs by Ion Implantation
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The channeling of ions near the GaAs <001> axis was investigated using 380 keV He<sup>+</sup>, 200 keV N<sup>+</sup> and Ne<sup>+</sup> as incident ions. Ion channeling has a detrimental effect on the uniformity of GaAs-FET V<inf>th</inf>, because the angle of the incident ion beam to the wafer varies during beam scanning in ion implantation. The sloped V<inf>th</inf>. distribution which is often observed in Si-implanted 2-inch wafers is well elucidated by ion channeling when we take into account the fact that the critical angle for the channeling of heavier ions with low energy is greater than that of lighter ions with high energy. Varying the tilt angle from 6° to 10°, we succeeded in reducing the standard deviation of the threshold voltage from 103 mV to 43 mV at an average threshold voltage of -1.5V. The use of an ingot-annealed substrate and ion implantation at a tilt angle of 9 further improved uniformity of V<inf>th</inf> to 27 mV at V<inf>th</inf>,=-1.06 V throughout the 2-inch wafer.

articleTitle: A Self-Aligned GaAs/AlGaAs Heterojunction Bipolar Transistor with V-Groove Isolated Planar Structure
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A novel self-aligned base structure for GaAs/AlGaAs Heterojunction Bipolar Transistors (HBTs) with a buried V-groove isolation has been proposed and achieved. It has a low base resistance and junction capacitances due to self-aligned p<sup>+</sup>- implanted extrinsic base with an emitter electrode. It also has a planar structure due to a V-groove buried-Si<inf>3</inf>N<inf>4</inf> device isolation technique which is suitable for large-scale integration. The high-speed performances are discussed using a two-dimensional device simulation and a SPICE circuit simulation. The result has indicated that a frequency divider implemented with this HBT will achieve a maximum input frequency of more than 20 GHz.

articleTitle: Divide by 128/129 5 mW 400 MHz Band GaAs Prescaler IC
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A 400MHz band GaAs 128/129 modulus prescaler IC was fabricated using a self-aligned WN gate technology. It exhibited 5mW minimum power operation at supply voltages down to IV. Power saving was achieved by employing DCFL (Direct Coupled FET Logic) circuits and optimizing FET channel lengths in the IC. A new flip-flop circuit configuration keeps the IC stable for supply voltages in the range IV to 2V at temperatures of -30°C to +80°C. The IC consists of 93 gates. The die size is 1.0mm × 1.2mm.

articleTitle: GaAs Jfet Technology for DCFL LSI
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper describes a GaAs JFET LSI technology applying to the fabrication of fully functional 1800 NOR gates. The LSI is composed of an 8×8 bit parallel multiplier and a 20 bit accumulator using a direct coupled FET logic (DCFL) circuit. The threshold voltage of a JFET can be precisely controlled during the junction formation using an on-chip threshold monitor. In addition, JFET's built with gate fingers in the [011] crystallographic orientation display small threshold deviations. The side-wall technology makes possible to open a sub-micron gate window. Fully functional 8×8 bit multiplier with accumulator has been built and displayed an average operation time of 7.6 nsec with a power dissipation of 609 mW, when operated at a supply voltage of 1.29 V. The minimum multiplication time of 5.6 nsec has been obtained at a supply voltage of 1.45 V.

articleTitle: New Dry Recess Etching Technology for GaAs Digital ICs
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A dry recess technology that is compatible with a self-aligned E/D MESFET IC process on 3 in. GaAs wafers for gate lengths 1 µm and below is presented. A unique self-limiting gate recess process called SLICE is used to maintain voltage threshold control and across-wafer uniformity of E-MESFETs. Using the dry gate recess E-MESFET, we have successfully fabricated state-of-the-art high transconductance E-MESFETs, E/D ring oscillators and E/D DCFL dividers.

articleTitle: Parameter Control in Ion-Implanted GaAs Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The quality of GaAs substrate material has been considered to be a major limiting factor for the development of VLSI GaAs integrated circuits. Threshold variations across wafer have been reportedly affected by variations in dislocation density, residual impurity content, and deep level concentration. The quality of substrate material has improved to the point in the past few years that it is no longer possible to expect enhanced performance and yield in ion-implanted devices strictly on the basis of improved material purity and uniformity. In many cases process-related effects can explain the variations in device characteristics across wafers. The purpose of the following discussion is to describe the role that the material and process-related nonuniformities can have on GaAs device characteristics with emphasis on ion-implanted MESFET devices. Topics to be covered include the electronic properties of state-of-the-art LEC GaAs material, the effects of residual channeling and dopant distribution effects on device characteristics, the role of dislocations, and the tolerable limits required for VLSI GaAs.

articleTitle: A GaAs 12-Bit Digital-to-Analog Converter
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A GaAs 12-bit digital-to-analog converter (DAC) has been designed and implemented for converting Gword/s data into analog signals. The chip is fabricated in an all-depletion mode process and contains all necessary data amplifiers, data latches, current switches, clock amplifiers, and a deglitcher. The DAC exhibits a dc linearity of better than ±1/8LSB at the 12-bit level. When used to generate a sampled sinusoid during wafer-probe testing, the DAC showed a signal-to-harmonic distortion of better than 66 dBc at 10 Mwords/s. In high-frequency tests the DAC's MSB exhibits 10-90 % rise and fall times of 200 ps and shows very flat settling.

articleTitle: An ECL-Compatible GaAs E/D Mesfet 1K-Bit Static RAM
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A fully ECL-compatible GaAs E/D MESFET Ik-bit static RAM was designed, fabricated, and tested. DCFL is used for the memory array while BFL is utilized in the I/O buffers to provide an ECL 100K interface. The memory cell area is 774 µm<sup>2</sup>, the smallest GaAs static RAM cell ever reported. The chip size is 2.0 × 1.75 mm<sup>2</sup>. Fabrication of the 1k-bit RAM involves a fully-implanted two-threshold process with true double-level metal interconnection. State-of-the-art E-MESFET transconductance values as high as 300 mS/mm at room temperature (200 mS/mm typical) have been obtained, and E-MESFET threshold voltage standard deviations of 25 to 60 mV are typically observed across 2 inch slices. A minimum access time of 2.5 ns has been obtained with a total power dissipation of 1.2 W (memory array power dissipation is only ~ 40 mW). A measured output voltage swing of 750 mV across a 50 ohm load has been achieved.

articleTitle: Comparison of Microscopic Uniformity of Recently Developed Semi-Insulating Substrates for GaAs LSI by using 60µm × 60µm Pitch Mesfet Array
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: The microscopic distributions of V<inf>th</inf> in the three kinds of LEC substrates, i.e. conventional undoped, In doped, and ingot annealed LEC substrate, were examined using the advanced high density FET array. In the center of conventional LEC substrate, the clear cellular pattern of V^h corresponding to the dislocation network pattern was observed. In some In doped and ingot annealed LEC substrates, very excellent uniformities of V<inf>th</inf> were obtained and the standard deviations for 700 FETs were less than 15 mV. However, the irregular patterns of V<inf>th</inf> were found in the others and it was found that In doped or ingot annealed LEC substrares were not always uniform.

articleTitle: A Gallium Arsenide Decoder for Gigabit Rate Communication Links
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A GaAs decoder, capable of decoding a three level data sequence at data rates of one gigabit per second, has been fabricated and tested. The three level code provides a level transition at each bit time, enabling the clock to be recovered directly from the incoming data stream. The use of three levels also allows the data decoding logic to run at the bit rate, providing the ability to decode data at high speeds. Both analog and digital circuits have been successfully integrated on this chip. Function blocks including comparators, differential amplifiers and output buffer circuits were designed and demonstrated to be functional at speed, with temperature and bias stability. Fifty high speed Buffered FET Logic (BFL) logic gates, configured as shift registers, delay chains and decoding logic, were used to regenerate the gigabit per second clock pulses and data bits from the detected levels.

articleTitle: Monolithic 1.6 Gbit/s 8:1 Multiplexer and 1:8 Demultiplexer Subsystems using CDFL
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This paper describes a fully ECL compatible 1.6 Gbit/s multiplexer (MUX) and companion demultiplexer (DEMUX) intended for use in fiber optic communication systems, RF memories, and high speed display applications. The circuits were fabricated using GigaBit's standard planar GaAs IC process, and characterized with respect to system performance. Each chip has approximately 200 equivalent logic gates and a power dissipation less than 1.5 W at the 1.6 GHz clock frequency. The Capacitor Diode-Coupled FET Logic (CDFL) approach was used to achieve good speed power product performance.

articleTitle: Circuit Performance of GaAlAs/GaAs Heterostructure Bipolar Junction Transistors
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: This extended abstract describes a theoretical evaluation of the performance of heterostructure bipolar junction transistors (HBT, GaAIAs/GaAs system) in emitter-coupled logic (ECL) and Schottky transistor logic (STL) circuits under loaded and unloaded conditions in order to obtain a comparison for large circuit applications and in order to understand their limiting features. Under loaded conditions, for 1 ftm minimum rules, ECL circuits show less than 60 pS delay at 4 mW/gate dissipation while STL circuits show less than 150 pS delay at .4 mW/gate dissipation. Structures with self-alignment should improve this limit to 40 pS and 120 pS respectively. Circuits are limited by transition capacitances and resistances. Diffusion capacitances are minimal in beterostructures at nominal current densities below 1 × 10<sup>5</sup> A/cm<sup>2</sup>. Any improvement in performance, thus, depends critically on technological innovations leading to reduction in capacitances and resistances. Offset voltages will have to be maintained below 100 mV. STL circuits, when driven at higher power, show delays of 50 to 65 pS at 1.2 mW/gate dissipation. This is comparable to ECL performance and will be limited by the quality of Schottky diodes that can be made on compound semiconductors.

articleTitle: A GaAs Laser-Driver Operating up to 2Gbit/s Data Rate
publicationTitle: 1985 IEEE GaAs IC Symposium Technical Digest
abstract: A high speed GaAs monolithic laser driver IC for application to high data-rate optical communication systems is demonstrated. The IC is designed to operate from DC to 2 Gbit/s with a compatible input level to Si ECL's at low data rates. Experimental IC's exhibited current driving capability of 50 mA p-p with a rise/fall time of 100 ps at 2 Gbit/s data rate.
